c1-m1.summary: The user is seeking new book recommendations.
c1-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm looking for some new book recommendations. Can you help me?
Assistant: Of course! I'd be happy to help you find some new books to read. What genre are you interested in?
User: Hmm, I'm not really sure. I've been feeling a bit stuck in a rut lately and I'm open to trying something new.
Assistant: Okay, well, let's explore some different options then. Have you read any books recently that you've really enjoyed?
User: Actually, I haven't had a lot of time to read lately, but I did re-read one of my old favorites over the holidays.
Assistant: Re-reading old favorites can be a great way to get back into reading. What was the book that you re-read?
User: It was a fantasy novel that I've loved since I was a teenager.
Assistant: Fantasy is a great genre! There are so many amazing books and authors to choose from. Did you have a favorite part or character in the book that you re-read?
User: Yeah, I've always loved the world-building in fantasy novels. I find it really immersive and engaging.
Assistant: World-building is definitely a key part of what makes fantasy novels so compelling. Are you looking for more books with a similar type of world-building?
User: Yeah, that would be great. I've also been thinking about trying to find more books that are similar to the ones I loved when I was younger.
Assistant: Nostalgic reading can be a lot of fun! It's great that you're looking to recapture some of that magic. As someone who loves fantasy books, are you looking for any specific type of fantasy, such as high fantasy, urban fantasy, or epic fantasy?
User: Hmm, I think I'd say high fantasy is my favorite. This person is a fantasy book lover, and I think that's why I've been having trouble finding new books to read - nothing seems to live up to the standards set by my old favorites!
Assistant: High fantasy can be a bit of a tough genre to break into, but there are definitely some amazing authors and books out there. I think I can help you find some new titles that might scratch that high fantasy itch. Would you be interested in some personalized recommendations?
User: That would be amazing, thank you! I'd love to hear some recommendations.
Assistant: Based on your love of high fantasy and world-building, I think you might enjoy authors like Patrick Rothfuss, Brandon Sanderson, or N.K. Jemisin. Have you read any of their books before?
User: Actually, I've been meaning to check out Patrick Rothfuss for a while now. I've heard great things about his books.
Assistant: The Kingkiller Chronicle series is definitely a great place to start. It's a high fantasy epic with amazing world-building and characters. I think you'll really enjoy it. Would you like more recommendations or would you like to start with that series?
User: Hi, I've been feeling a bit stuck lately and I'm not sure what to do with my free time.
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what you mean by "stuck"? Are you feeling bored or unfulfilled?
User: Yeah, I guess I'm just feeling like I'm not doing anything meaningful or exciting. I'm looking for something to shake things up.

User: Actually, I've been thinking about exploring my creative side more. I've always been fascinated by people who can create art or music from scratch.

User: Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: What is the impact of fantasy sports on workplace productivity?

Passage: The everyman's obsession that lets everyone be the owner of a pro-ball team is big business.
NEW YORK (FORTUNE) - The American male's obsession with sports is nothing new, but try this on for size: More than half of fantasy sports fanatics spend over an hour a day just thinking about their teams.
That finding, along with the fact that one in four fantasy players spends more than $500 a year on the games, comes from the first-ever sociological analysis of online fantasy sports participants, conducted by Don Levy, an assistant sociology professor at West Virginia Wesleyan College.
These games, burgeoning in popularity and run by Web sites like ESPN.com and CBS SportsLine, allow regular Joes to create and run teams of actual professional athletes in sports like baseball and football. The teams square off against each other in leagues formed by friends or workmates, with teams earning points based on the on-field performance of, say, Derek Jeter or Peyton Manning.
With upwards of 15 million players in the U.S., fantasy sports are a billion-dollar market. CBS SportsLine, for example, generated $15 million in sales from 1.3 million fantasy football customers last year.
Since fantasy players tend to linger on sites -- reading player profiles, pondering their starting lineups, and sending messages to others in the league -- they attract blue-chip advertisers like McDonald's (up $0.10 to $35.26, Research), Verizon (down $0.29 to $31.45, Research) and General Motors (up $0.65 to $23.04, Research).
Responding to fantasy players' insatiable desire for content, CBS and ESPN are also doing more to incorporate fantasy storylines and themes in their TV coverage of sporting events.
Who is the fantasy sports fanatic?
While fantasy's viability as a business is now unquestioned, little has been heretofore known about the people who play fantasy sports.
For starters, the one-year study, made exclusive to FORTUNE Magazine, found that they're mostly male, white, married, well-educated (over two-thirds of Levy's sample had a college degree or better) and earn a decent living.
Of the nearly 1,200 people queried, three out of four earn at least $50,000 a year, well above the national average.
"These are not social misfits living in their parents' basement," said Levy. Not surprisingly, the majority rated their sports "fanship" very high, with fanship being defined as active consumption of sport.
Most interesting, though, was Levy's finding that 60 percent of fantasy players spend over an hour a day just thinking about their fantasy team, and 85 percent spent over 30 minutes.
Granted, Levy's sample was skewed towards rabid fantasy players like Larry Dobrow, 35, a Manhattan-based freelance writer who thinks the one-hour-a-day figure may be understated.
"During the days leading up to a baseball or football draft, [fantasy] is pretty much your primary concern -- including work, relationships, and sometimes hygiene," he said.
Workplace consultancy Challenger, Gray & Christmas estimates that fantasy football alone will cost employers $196.1 million in lost productivity during the current NFL season. That figure may prove to be conservative, since it was based on fantasy players taking only 10 minutes out of their work day to manage their teams.
"Productivity goes down the drain," said CEO John Challenger. "It's like a virus."
Despite the impact on productivity, Challenger says companies shouldn't quash fantasy participation during work hours, as the effects of a ban could be far worse than the damage caused by playing fantasy games.
Levy's study quantifies that damage: Two-thirds of his sample spend at least five hours a week managing their fantasy teams, and more than an third are busy with fantasy sports for more than 10 hours a week. Those hours can come at any time. During his eight-day Mediterranean honeymoon cruise, Mark Del Franco, 36, recalled logging onto the ship's Internet connection to make daily lineup changes. "At that point, my wife was asking herself if she made a mistake," he said.
The damage extends to fantasy players' wallets as well. Since most players pony up dollars not only for league entry fees but also subscribe to fantasy news and analysis sites, the money spent by fantasy players annually can really add up. The average amount spent was $360, Levy found, but 24 percent spend more than $500 a year on their various teams.
Levy argues that while sports do not take over the lives of these fans, sport -- and the consumption of sports news, games and information -- was "laced throughout the day's structure" and as such, "has become the language of men and masculinity."
Nearly half spend more than 10 hours a week watching sports on TV, which is perhaps not news to the spouses of these men.
The study also investigated why they play. For starters, it's fun. It also makes watching sports more interesting.
Others like the competition and the ever-present trash talking on league message boards. Less important, Levy found, was using fantasy sports to meet new people or to satisfy a thirst for gambling.
And for those who think that hours spent on fantasy Web sites will rot your brain, fear not. Levy argues that fantasy sports success depends to some degree on the use of abstraction, rationality and the employment of positivism.
While 82 percent played an organized sport in high school or beyond, having played the game is not a prerequisite for fantasy success. Rather, those who do well don't get wrapped up in the real-life moral foibles of professional players -- what that player can do for him on the field is more important than what kind of person he is.
"Some would call this approach businesslike," Levy writes.
So do many corporate chieftains play fantasy football? The only one we could find was Doug Brooks, CEO of Brinker International (up $0.27 to $40.66, Research), parent company of restaurant chain Chili's, whose fantasy football team, as of week 13, remained winless.
But his company's stock is up 7 percent since the start of the football season, so shareholders can rest assured that his mind is squarely on Brinker.
The ESPN lifestyle has arrived. Click here for more.
Can "Moneyball" survive? Click here for more.

NEW YORK (FORTUNE) - The American male's obsession with sports is nothing new, but try this on for size: More than half of fantasy sports fanatics spend over an hour a day just thinking about their teams.
That finding, along with the fact that one in four fantasy players spends more than $500 a year on the games, comes from the first-ever sociological analysis of online fantasy sports participants, conducted by Don Levy, an assistant sociology professor at West Virginia Wesleyan College.
These games, burgeoning in popularity and run by Web sites like ESPN.com and CBS SportsLine, allow regular Joes to create and run teams of actual professional athletes in sports like baseball and football. The teams square off against each other in leagues formed by friends or workmates, with teams earning points based on the on-field performance of, say, Derek Jeter or Peyton Manning.
With upwards of 15 million players in the U.S., fantasy sports are a billion-dollar market. CBS SportsLine, for example, generated $15 million in sales from 1.3 million fantasy football customers last year.
Since fantasy players tend to linger on sites -- reading player profiles, pondering their starting lineups, and sending messages to others in the league -- they attract blue-chip advertisers like McDonald's (up $0.10 to $35.26, Research), Verizon (down $0.29 to $31.45, Research) and General Motors (up $0.65 to $23.04, Research).
Responding to fantasy players' insatiable desire for content, CBS and ESPN are also doing more to incorporate fantasy storylines and themes in their TV coverage of sporting events.
Who is the fantasy sports fanatic?
While fantasy's viability as a business is now unquestioned, little has been heretofore known about the people who play fantasy sports.
For starters, the one-year study, made exclusive to FORTUNE Magazine, found that they're mostly male, white, married, well-educated (over two-thirds of Levy's sample had a college degree or better) and earn a decent living.
Of the nearly 1,200 people queried, three out of four earn at least $50,000 a year, well above the national average.
"These are not social misfits living in their parents' basement," said Levy. Not surprisingly, the majority rated their sports "fanship" very high, with fanship being defined as active consumption of sport.
Most interesting, though, was Levy's finding that 60 percent of fantasy players spend over an hour a day just thinking about their fantasy team, and 85 percent spent over 30 minutes.
Granted, Levy's sample was skewed towards rabid fantasy players like Larry Dobrow, 35, a Manhattan-based freelance writer who thinks the one-hour-a-day figure may be understated.
"During the days leading up to a baseball or football draft, [fantasy] is pretty much your primary concern -- including work, relationships, and sometimes hygiene," he said.
Workplace consultancy Challenger, Gray & Christmas estimates that fantasy football alone will cost employers $196.1 million in lost productivity during the current NFL season. That figure may prove to be conservative, since it was based on fantasy players taking only 10 minutes out of their work day to manage their teams.
"Productivity goes down the drain," said CEO John Challenger. "It's like a virus."
Despite the impact on productivity, Challenger says companies shouldn't quash fantasy participation during work hours, as the effects of a ban could be far worse than the damage caused by playing fantasy games.
Levy's study quantifies that damage: Two-thirds of his sample spend at least five hours a week managing their fantasy teams, and more than an third are busy with fantasy sports for more than 10 hours a week. Those hours can come at any time. During his eight-day Mediterranean honeymoon cruise, Mark Del Franco, 36, recalled logging onto the ship's Internet connection to make daily lineup changes. "At that point, my wife was asking herself if she made a mistake," he said.
The damage extends to fantasy players' wallets as well. Since most players pony up dollars not only for league entry fees but also subscribe to fantasy news and analysis sites, the money spent by fantasy players annually can really add up. The average amount spent was $360, Levy found, but 24 percent spend more than $500 a year on their various teams.
Levy argues that while sports do not take over the lives of these fans, sport -- and the consumption of sports news, games and information -- was "laced throughout the day's structure" and as such, "has become the language of men and masculinity."
Nearly half spend more than 10 hours a week watching sports on TV, which is perhaps not news to the spouses of these men.
The study also investigated why they play. For starters, it's fun. It also makes watching sports more interesting.
Others like the competition and the ever-present trash talking on league message boards. Less important, Levy found, was using fantasy sports to meet new people or to satisfy a thirst for gambling.
And for those who think that hours spent on fantasy Web sites will rot your brain, fear not. Levy argues that fantasy sports success depends to some degree on the use of abstraction, rationality and the employment of positivism.
While 82 percent played an organized sport in high school or beyond, having played the game is not a prerequisite for fantasy success. Rather, those who do well don't get wrapped up in the real-life moral foibles of professional players -- what that player can do for him on the field is more important than what kind of person he is.
"Some would call this approach businesslike," Levy writes.
So do many corporate chieftains play fantasy football? The only one we could find was Doug Brooks, CEO of Brinker International (up $0.27 to $40.66, Research), parent company of restaurant chain Chili's, whose fantasy football team, as of week 13, remained winless.
But his company's stock is up 7 percent since the start of the football season, so shareholders can rest assured that his mind is squarely on Brinker.

This attention to setting creates a unique and captivating world for readers, and contributes to the overall success of the work of fiction.

2. Space Opera: This subgenre is characterized by sprawling settings that take place across entire galaxies, often featuring epic battles and political intrigue. The setting is a huge part of the appeal of space opera, and is often what draws readers in. The intricate world-building and attention to detail in the setting contributes to the success of the work of fiction.

3. High Fantasy: This subgenre takes place in a world that is completely different from our own, often featuring magical creatures, ancient lore, and epic battles between good and evil. The setting is crucial to high fantasy, as it creates a sense of wonder and escapism for readers. The more detailed and immersive the setting, the more successful the work of fiction is likely to be.

Overall, a strong emphasis on setting can greatly contribute to the success of a work of fantasy or sci-fi, as it creates a unique and immersive world for readers to explore. This can result in a stronger emotional connection to the characters and story, as well as a sense of wonder and escapism that is often associated with these genres.

User: Which subgenres of fantasy or sci-fi prioritize setting the most, and how does this affect their overall success as a work of fiction?
Assistant: There are several subgenres of fantasy or sci-fi that prioritize setting:

1. Steampunk: This subgenre takes place in a setting heavily inspired by Victorian-era technology, with steam power and clockwork mechanisms. The setting is often as important as the characters and story itself, and is very descriptive and immersive. This attention to setting creates a unique and captivating world for readers, and contributes to the overall success of the work of fiction.

2. Space Opera: This subgenre is characterized by sprawling settings that take place across entire galaxies, often featuring epic battles and political intrigue. The setting is a huge part of the appeal of space opera, and is often what draws readers in. The intricate world-building and attention to detail in the setting contributes to the success of the work of fiction.

3. High Fantasy: This subgenre takes place in a world that is completely different from our own, often featuring magical creatures, ancient lore, and epic battles between good and evil. The setting is crucial to high fantasy, as it creates a sense of wonder and escapism for readers. The more detailed and immersive the setting, the more successful the work of fiction is likely to be.

Overall, a strong emphasis on setting can greatly contribute to the success of a work of fantasy or sci-fi, as it creates a unique and immersive world for readers to explore. This can result in a stronger emotional connection to the characters and story, as well as a sense of wonder and escapism that is often associated with these genres.
User: Interesting, but what about genres that don't prioritize setting as much? Can they still be successful works of fantasy or sci-fi?
Assistant: Yes, absolutely! Other subgenres may place less emphasis on setting, but instead focus more on themes, characters, or plot. For example:

1. Urban Fantasy: This subgenre is often set in contemporary, real-world settings with magical or supernatural elements. Instead of creating a completely original world, urban fantasy relies on the reader's existing knowledge of the real world and adds in magical elements. While setting is still important, it is not the primary focus. Instead, the genre often prioritizes character development and exploring themes of good vs. Evil or the supernatural world vs. The mundane.

2. Hard Sci-Fi: This subgenre is focused on exploring scientific concepts and technology in a realistic and believable way. While there may be imaginative settings, the story is largely focused on exploring the science behind it. Its success may come more from the accuracy of the science portrayed or how it is used to drive the plot, rather than the setting.

3. Cyberpunk: This subgenre takes place in a setting heavily influenced by technology and often takes place in distopian or corporate-controlled world. While setting is important, the genre is often more concerned with exploring themes of social inequality or the impact of technology on society.

In conclusion, while setting can be an important element to the success of works of fiction in the fantasy and sci-fi genre, it is not the only factor. Other subgenres can prioritize themes, characters, and plot over setting, and still be highly successful.
User: What about genres that mix a variety of elements, such as magic and technology, in their setting? How do they differ from the others in terms of prioritizing setting?
Assistant: Genres that mix a variety of elements, such as magic and technology, in their settings, tend to prioritize their settings differently. Such genres are often referred to as "hybrid genres," "mixed genres," or "genre blends."

The way that such genres prioritize setting depends on the unique combination of elements they use, but often they emphasize the world-building as a whole, rather than just the magic or technology. 

For instance, the setting in a steampunk or clockpunk work is heavily influenced by the technology of the time period it is recreating, but also features magical or fantastical elements that would not ordinarily exist in the real world. This means that the setting in these subgenres is critical to building the world as a whole, and both magic and technology are given equal attention.

Similarly, in a genre like urban fantasy that incorporates both magical and technological elements, the world-building is critical to the success of the work of fiction. Readers must understand how the magic and technology work together and how they affect the world in which the story takes place. In such genres, storyline, character development, and writing style often complements the setting, rather than the other way around, making the setting all the more crucial to the novel's success.

In summary, hybrid genres often prioritize setting as a major element in tying everything together, allowing the reader to visualize and understand the unique combination of magic and technology. The quality of execution, world-building, and attention to technical and fantastic details become more important in such genres.
User: It's fascinating to see how different subgenres approach world-building and setting, but do you think that some genres rely too heavily on setting at the expense of other elements, like character development or plot?
Assistant: Yes, there is certainly the potential for some genres to rely so heavily on setting that other important elements, such as character development or plot, become overshadowed or neglected. It's important for writers to remember that no matter how fascinating or immersive the setting of their story may be, it is the characters and their actions that ultimately drive the narrative.

For example, a world with detailed magical systems or futuristic technology may be intriguing on its own, but without strong characters to inhabit it and an engaging plot to tie everything together, the story can fall flat.

That being said, a well-realized setting can enhance the characters and plot in many ways. A thoughtfully developed setting, with its own unique history, language, or culture, can add depth and complexity to characters by creating a rich backdrop or context in which they operate. It can also provide opportunities for characters to confront obstacles or navigate situations unique to that world, creating opportunities for character growth and developing the plot.

In summary, while setting is an important aspect of world-building, other elements such as character development and plot are equally important for the success of a work of fiction. A well-realized setting can complement and enhance these other elements, but cannot substitute them on its own.

Assistant: If you're in the mood for science fiction, I would recommend starting with "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy" by Douglas Adams. This book is a timeless classic that has entertained people for decades with its wit, humor, and imaginative take on the sci-fi genre. The book follows the misadventures of an unwitting traveler named Arthur Dent and his alien friend Ford Prefect as they travel through space and time. The book is a satire of many aspects of modern life and is sure to leave you laughing out loud. Happy reading!
User: Hey, the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy sounds like a fun read! Do you have any other humorous science fiction recommendations? I'm looking for something that will make me laugh out loud.
Assistant: Absolutely! If you're looking for more humorous science fiction books, here are a few extra recommendations to consider:

1. "Red Dwarf" by Grant Naylor: This is a series of books (and a TV show) that follows the adventures of Dave Lister, a man who wakes up from suspended animation to find that he is the last living human being on a space ship called the Red Dwarf. The books are full of humor, absurdity, and bizarre situations.

2. "The Stainless Steel Rat" by Harry Harrison: This series follows a criminal mastermind named James Bolivar diGriz, aka "Slippery Jim," who uses his skills to pull off daring heists and get out of sticky situations. The books are full of witty banter, clever schemes, and memorable characters.

3. "Cat's Cradle" by Kurt Vonnegut: This book is a satirical take on science (fiction) and religion, and follows the narrator as he investigates the life of a deceased scientist who helped develop the atomic bomb. The book is full of absurdity, dark humor, and thought-provoking ideas.

4. "Good Omens" by Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman: This book is a hilarious take on the Apocalypse, and follows an angel and a demon who team up to prevent the end of the world. The book is full of witty dialogue, quirky characters, and absurd situations.

I hope these recommendations make you laugh out loud while also satisfying your craving for sci-fi!

That being said, "Good Omens" by Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman is also incredibly funny, so if you're in the mood for a book that is both witty and satirical, that one might be a great choice too. Ultimately, it depends on your personal taste, but I hope you enjoy whichever book you choose!

It’s part of a trilogy following the original three movies. “Rogue One” arrived in theaters Dec. 16 and grossed more than $440 million in North America and about $800 million globally in its first 20 days. Question/Instruction: What were some of the factors that contributed to the enduring popularity of the Star Wars franchise?

Given material: The following article is entirely the opinion of Deanna Chapman and does not reflect the views of the Inquisitr.
Star Wars Celebration is an event that is taking place in Orlando, Florida, this year. The event started today and will run through Sunday. They are currently celebrating 40 years of Star Wars and today, they also presented a tribute to Carrie Fisher.
Carrie Fisher, known as Princess Leia to Star Wars fans, passed away in December, 2016. We know that her filming was completed for Star Wars: The Last Jedi and that there’s no doubt she’d appear in it. She is survived by Billie Lourd, who made an appearance at Star Wars Celebration. She made a brief appearance in Star Wars: The Force Awakens as Lieutenant Connix. She will reprise the role in The Last Jedi. Anthony Breznican from Entertainment Weekly reported on what Billie Lourd had to say about her mother.
The fact that Star Wars is still immensely popular after 40 years is a huge testament to what George Lucas built when he created this whole fictional universe. You can go so far down the rabbit hole with Star Wars just to learn about each person, planet, or creature. It’s amazing how much detail went into the original movie and how much detail continues to go into this universe.
George Lucas and Kathleen Kennedy both made appearances for the tribute. If you listen to them, you can tell just how much Carrie Fisher means to Star Wars and to each of them personally. They went all out on this tribute and it is well deserved for Carrie Fisher. Her personality shone through in the first trilogy and she gave everything she had in The Force Awakens. I’m anxiously awaiting The Last Jedi just to see how she closes out her performance as Princess Leia.
Star Wars is something that people enjoy immensely and casually. Sure, there are people who don’t pay any attention to Star Wars, but millions do. And it is people around the world who pay attention to it. A lot of franchises will fizzle out after one or two sequels or only see huge success in one country, but Star Wars stays strong. They’re celebrating 40 years with good reason. With the way Lucasfilm is reviving the Star Wars franchise, we can expect more movies for the foreseeable future.
There’s been some talk about whether or not Carrie Fisher will play Princess Leia again in future movies. Personally, I wouldn’t be a fan of that. Having her appear briefly in Rogue One already caused a bit of disapproval from fans, so they like won’t use her past what she completed filming prior to her death. Plus, it would put a dent in their budget to try to digitally recreate her character.
Carrie Fisher was much more than Princess Leia. She was a writer, as well, and she did it well. She made mistakes and had no problem cracking jokes about them and owning up to them. Her personality really was something that came through in everything she did. Her candidness made her feel extremely accessible and relatable. There will never again be someone like Carrie Fisher. And no one else will have quite the same impact on Star Wars as she did.
Star Wars: The Last Jedi will be out this December.

Question/Instruction: What were some of the factors that contributed to the enduring popularity of the Star Wars franchise?

Given material: The following article is entirely the opinion of Deanna Chapman and does not reflect the views of the Inquisitr.
Star Wars Celebration is an event that is taking place in Orlando, Florida, this year. The event started today and will run through Sunday. They are currently celebrating 40 years of Star Wars and today, they also presented a tribute to Carrie Fisher.
Carrie Fisher, known as Princess Leia to Star Wars fans, passed away in December, 2016. We know that her filming was completed for Star Wars: The Last Jedi and that there’s no doubt she’d appear in it. She is survived by Billie Lourd, who made an appearance at Star Wars Celebration. She made a brief appearance in Star Wars: The Force Awakens as Lieutenant Connix. She will reprise the role in The Last Jedi. Anthony Breznican from Entertainment Weekly reported on what Billie Lourd had to say about her mother.
The fact that Star Wars is still immensely popular after 40 years is a huge testament to what George Lucas built when he created this whole fictional universe. You can go so far down the rabbit hole with Star Wars just to learn about each person, planet, or creature. It’s amazing how much detail went into the original movie and how much detail continues to go into this universe.
George Lucas and Kathleen Kennedy both made appearances for the tribute. If you listen to them, you can tell just how much Carrie Fisher means to Star Wars and to each of them personally. They went all out on this tribute and it is well deserved for Carrie Fisher. Her personality shone through in the first trilogy and she gave everything she had in The Force Awakens. I’m anxiously awaiting The Last Jedi just to see how she closes out her performance as Princess Leia.
Star Wars is something that people enjoy immensely and casually. Sure, there are people who don’t pay any attention to Star Wars, but millions do. And it is people around the world who pay attention to it. A lot of franchises will fizzle out after one or two sequels or only see huge success in one country, but Star Wars stays strong. They’re celebrating 40 years with good reason. With the way Lucasfilm is reviving the Star Wars franchise, we can expect more movies for the foreseeable future.
There’s been some talk about whether or not Carrie Fisher will play Princess Leia again in future movies. Personally, I wouldn’t be a fan of that. Having her appear briefly in Rogue One already caused a bit of disapproval from fans, so they like won’t use her past what she completed filming prior to her death. Plus, it would put a dent in their budget to try to digitally recreate her character.
Carrie Fisher was much more than Princess Leia. She was a writer, as well, and she did it well. She made mistakes and had no problem cracking jokes about them and owning up to them. Her personality really was something that came through in everything she did. Her candidness made her feel extremely accessible and relatable. There will never again be someone like Carrie Fisher. And no one else will have quite the same impact on Star Wars as she did.
Star Wars: The Last Jedi will be out this December.

User: Hmm, that's a great question. I think I want to go for something neon and bold. I love how neon lights up under the black lights, and it's just so... rave-y!
Assistant: Neon is a fantastic choice! It's definitely a classic rave look. Have you considered adding any fun accessories to really make your outfit pop? Like, have you thought about hats, sunglasses, or jewelry?
User: Oh, totally! I love accessorizing. I'm actually thinking of making some of my own accessories, like glow-in-the-dark flower crowns or LED-infused sunglasses. Planning my next rave or music festival outfit and accessories is a fun way for me to express my creativity and showcase my love for electronic music.
Assistant: Wow, that sounds like an amazing project! I love that you're taking the time to create something truly unique and personalized. Do you have any tips or tricks for someone who might be looking to create their own festival accessories? What materials or tools do you like to use?
User: Definitely! I think the key is to just have fun with it and experiment with different materials and techniques. I love using fabric paint, glitter, and, of course, glow-in-the-dark accents. And don't be afraid to get creative with DIY tutorials online or just winging it and seeing what happens.
Assistant: That's such great advice. And I'm sure your hard work will pay off when you're dancing the night away, looking and feeling like a total rockstar. What's the most important thing for you when it comes to creating your festival look? Is it comfort, self-expression, or something else entirely?
User: For me, it's all about self-expression and having fun with it. I love how festivals give you the freedom to let loose and be yourself, without judgment. And, of course, I want to make sure I'm comfortable enough to dance the night away!
Assistant: I couldn't agree more! It's all about embracing the festival spirit and letting your personality shine through. Well, I'm sure you'll have an amazing time at the rave, and I'm excited to hear all about it afterwards!
User: Hey, what's up? I just got back from an awesome concert last night. The DJ was insane!
Assistant: That sounds like a blast! I'm glad you had a great time. Electronic music is so much fun live, isn't it? The energy of the crowd, the bass thumping through your chest...
User: Exactly! I love the way the lights and music just take over. I've been listening to a lot of electronic music lately, and I'm starting to appreciate the different layers and textures in the songs.
Assistant: Yeah, electronic music is all about the production quality. The artists put so much work into crafting the perfect sound. Do you have a favorite artist or song that you've been listening to on repeat?
User: Actually, I've been getting into some older Daft Punk albums. Their sound is so unique and ahead of its time. I love how they blend disco and house elements with futuristic synths.
Assistant: Daft Punk is a great choice! They're definitely pioneers in the electronic music scene. Have you ever thought about how their music would sound in a home setting? Like, if you were to set up a sound system that could do justice to their productions?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I've never really thought about it, but now that you mention it, I think it would be awesome to have a sound system that could replicate the energy of a live concert.
Assistant: Absolutely! Having a good sound system can completely change the way you experience music. And with electronic music, it's all about the details – the punchy bass, the crisp highs, the nuanced textures... A good sound system can bring out all those elements and transport you to another world.
User: That's so true. I frequently think about upgrading my home music setup to ensure I have the best possible sound quality to enjoy my favorite electronic music. But I'm not sure where to start or what to look for in a sound system.
Assistant: Well, let's break it down! First, you'll want to consider the size of your room and the type of speakers that would work best in that space. Then, you can think about the components you need – a good amp, a subwoofer for that deep bass, maybe some bookshelf speakers for a more immersive experience...
User: Okay, that makes sense. But what about the technical aspects? I've heard terms like "frequency response" and "signal-to-noise ratio" thrown around, but I have no idea what they mean or how to apply them to my setup.
Assistant: Don't worry, it's not as complicated as it sounds! Frequency response refers to the range of frequencies that a speaker can produce – so, if a speaker has a frequency response of 20Hz-20kHz, that means it can produce sounds as low as 20Hz (which is really deep bass) and as high as 20kHz (which is really high treble). Signal-to-noise ratio, on the other hand, refers to how much background noise a speaker produces compared to the actual music. A higher signal-to-noise ratio means a cleaner, more accurate sound.
User: Alright, I think I'm starting to get it. But what about the actual process of setting up a sound system? I've heard it can be a real pain to get everything connected and calibrated properly.
Assistant: Yeah, it can be a bit of a challenge, but it's worth it in the end! I can walk you through a step-by-step guide if you'd like. We can start with the basics – connecting your speakers to your amp, setting up your subwoofer, and adjusting the levels to get the perfect balance...

User: What are some common production techniques used in EDM music?
Assistant: 1. Sampling: This technique involves taking portions of audio from other tracks and incorporating them into your own.

2. Synthesizers: Synthesizers are electronic instruments that generate sound through the use of oscillators and filters. They are used extensively in EDM production to create unique sounds and melodies.

3. Drum Machines: Drum machines are electronic devices that can produce a wide range of percussion sounds. These are commonly used in EDM tracks to create high-energy rhythms.

4. Compression: Compression is a process that levels out the volume of different elements in a track. This ensures that all elements are heard at the same volume and prevents any one element from overpowering the mix.

5. Equalization: Equalization is the process of adjusting the frequency balance of a mix. This can be used to make certain elements stand out more or to remove unwanted frequencies.

6. Reverb: Reverb is an effect that simulates the natural echo and reflection of a sound in a room. This is commonly used in EDM to create a sense of space and depth in the mix.

7. Delay: Delay creates echoes of a sound by repeating it at a set interval. This can be used to create unique rhythms and add movement to a track.

8. Sidechain Compression: This technique involves using a compressor to decrease the volume of one sound every time another sound plays. This can be used to create a pulsing effect in a track.

9. Automation: Automation involves changing the settings of a parameter over time. This can be used to create effects such as filter sweeps or modulations.

10. Layering: Layering involves combining multiple sounds together to create a more complex sound. This can be used to create unique melodies or to add depth to a track.
User: I've heard a lot about the "drop" in EDM tracks. How is that usually achieved in production?
Assistant: The "drop" is a key element in many EDM tracks, and it refers to the point in the track where the energy is released and the beat hits at its fullest. There are several ways to achieve a powerful drop in an EDM track, including:

1. Build-Up: A gradual rise in intensity through elements like percussion, vocal samples, and risers can lead up to the drop, building anticipation in the listener.

2. Silence: A sudden silence or break can create tension and anticipation for the drop to come.

3. Impactful Sound Design: Sounds like bass drops, heavy drums, and synths can create a powerful impact and give the drop its energy.

4. Arrangement: Precise arrangement of elements in the track, such as choosing the right tempo and key, can create a harmonious buildup and drop.

5. Effects: Effects such as reverb, delay, and filters can manipulate the sound and create a sense of space for the drop. 

Overall, the success of a drop is a combination of effective sound design, arrangement, and accumulation of energy through the track.
User: That's really interesting! Do producers usually plan out the drop beforehand or is it something that just happens naturally during the production process?
Assistant: EDM producers usually plan out the drop beforehand when producing a track. The drop is a significant part of an EDM track, and producers want it to be the highlight of the song. They usually have a general idea of how they want the drop to sound like, and they work towards it during the production process.

Producers will experiment with different synth patches, rhythms, and percussion to create a suitable build-up and drop combination. This experimentation process can take a while, and many producers will test out different approaches to the drop to find the one that works best.

Once they have an idea of how they want the drop to sound like, they will build the build-up towards it. They will usually create several iterations of the build-up and the drop to refine it as they progress through the production process, ensuring that everything sounds cohesive and powerful.

In summary, while it may happen naturally at times during the production process, most producers will plan out the drop beforehand to ensure they get the desired impact and energy they want in their track.

c81-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Who is the grim reaper?
To make an iconic series you need an iconic character. The hooded cape, the faceless form and let’s not forget that giant scythe, this guy is the icon of icons but historically there’s a problem, too scary. But the image is not the man. It’s a costume, uniform of the day job, a way for the bosses to create a monster to do their dirty work. The real Grim is an entirely different soul.
Look inside Grim's afterlife locker and you’ll find a beat box, a mixtape and some old skool memorabilia. Seems our hero was there back in the day, saw things going down in New York City circa '88. You see the true Grim lives for Hip Hop.
Don’t believe me? Look under the cape and you’ll find a pair of Adidas Ultrastar 80s, made to walk this way. And inside the hooded cape, sequins. Total bling.
Misread for millennia the Grim Reaper is sick of finding his sneakers in the trashcan, sick of hiding in the locker rooms of the afterlife so he's made up his mind to come clean and follow his dream. Understandably it’s not a popular decision – Grim Reapers don’t dance.
Undeterred by his boss’s disapproval Grim approaches a series of street dance crews but bad news travels fast and his attempts to reach out are greeted by empty rehearsal rooms, spinning disco balls and a lot of barren tongue and groove. Nobody wants to partner with… Death.
Seems the world isn’t able to see past the robes. Of course it’s easy to say don’t worry, big G’s not going to hurt you, but would you shake hands with seven feet of swirling nothing-ness? You’d need proof, right?
They have to learn to work together and that’s not easy if falling out is your only qualification. This combination of character faults will give us our comic sensibility and human tone. A tone that will make the audience root for our crew until the bitter end, also worrying it could go terribly wrong at any moment, classic edge of the seat storytelling.
With The Grim Reaper on your side, anything’s possible.
Of course there’s more than a little fantasy along the way. Without some supernatural moments we wouldn’t be able to see what really goes on in the afterlife and exactly how The Reapers manage their most essential of jobs. There’s time bending, alternative realities and a fair amount of strange goings on. But that’s nothing compared to what goes on in our world, which is truly extraordinary.
This is the story of one of the world’s most iconic characters, remixed for the 21st century. Could you continue the story by describing a specific incident where the Grim Reaper tries to join a street dance crew and faces rejection?
Assistant: Grim Reaper had set his mind on following his passion for hip hop, but the journey was not going to be easy. He knew that he needed to find a crew that would accept him for who he was, not just as the scary and intimidating figure that he portrayed.

He went from one dance studio to another, but the moment he entered the room, all activity came to a halt. The dancers, lost in their moves and rhythm, froze at the sight of Grim. They stared at him, horrified, unable to look past his robe and scythe.

Despite their initial shock, Grim approached the crew, determined to show them his love for hip hop. He told them about his passion for dancing, how he had even seen the birth of hip hop in the streets of New York City.

But it was all in vain. The crew, still intimidated by his presence, rejected him outright. They had no place for someone like Grim in their team, and they made it clear to him.

Heartbroken, Grim left the studio, his head bowed low. He had hoped that he could show the world that he was more than just a symbol of death, that he had a life beyond his robes and scythe. But his dream had been shattered, and he felt more alone than ever.

However, Grim was not one to give up easily. He knew that he had something special to offer, and he wasn't going to let a few rejections stop him. With renewed determination, he set out to find another crew, hoping this time they would see him for who he truly was.
User: Hey, I love this concept! Can you tell me more about the specific character traits and flaws of the Grim Reaper that make him relatable and human?
Assistant: Certainly! The Grim Reaper, despite his ominous and intimidating appearance, is just like any other person when you get down to it. Here are some of the character traits and flaws that make him relatable and human:

1. Passionate: The Grim Reaper is deeply passionate about hip hop, which is a surprising but endearing character trait. It shows that he has interests and hobbies beyond his job, and that he can be enthusiastic about something just like anyone else.

User: Here is a piece of text: Changing lanes: The state junior tenpin bowling team recently visited Bunbury for a training session. Photo: Thomas Munday.
The Tenpin Bowling Association of Western Australia will be sending 11 young athletes on an amazing adventure later this year.
The state junior team was put through its paces during a training session at Bunbury Ten Pin Bowl and Family Fun Centre on Sunday, February 3.
The group took part in a warm-up and completed multiple training drills.
In April, the team will head to Oz Tenpin, in Chirnside Park, Victoria, for the 2019 Australian Junior Masters competition.
The WA side currently has seven boys, all guided by state junior team boys manager Karen Scanlon.
Busselton tenpin bowler Connor Dallachy, 16, said he was thrilled to be on the team.
“I love how enjoyable the sport is, learning how to improve, and meeting new people,” he said.
“I will be training and practising every day prior to the tournament.
Assisted by state junior team girls manager Jamie Turner, the team has four female participants.
Three Queensland girls will represent WA during the upcoming tournament.
“To give them more experience, we’re moving the participants around to different centres in Western Australia,” Tuner said.
“They are getting to play on sets of lanes that most of them haven’t experienced before. They also get a weekend away in Bunbury.
“We usually get a couple of them to lead the warm-ups.
Turner said they were determined to hone their skills ahead of the event.
“Prior to the tournament, they will be training every Sunday morning and competing in various competitions,” he said.
“This will give them a bit more experience.
“They will be competing in singles, doubles, and four-person teams while we’re in Victoria.
“We want to make sure everyone gets along and works well in a team.
“We get to see how each individual bowler interacts with the other bowlers.
Turner said tenpin bowling was an enjoyable, engaging sport for people of all ages.
“My son – Blake Turner – has been playing in a league since he was six, and now he’s 12,” he said.
